:::{#exm-piecewise-constant-schedule}
#### A ten-fold drop twice

Take $s^{(0)} = 0.1$ and $\decay = 0.1$,
with drops at $t_1 = 30$ and $t_2 = 60$.
The [step length](#def-piecewise-constant-schedule) just before and at each drop is:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: piecewise-constant-schedule-r
#| code-fold: false
s0_pc <- 0.1
decay_pc <- 0.1
drops_pc <- c(30, 60)
t_pc <- c(0, 29, 30, 59, 60, 90)
k_pc <- colSums(outer(drops_pc, t_pc, "<="))
data.frame(t = t_pc, step_length = s0_pc * decay_pc^k_pc)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: piecewise-constant-schedule-python
#| code-fold: false
s0_pc, decay_pc, drops_pc = 0.1, 0.1, [30, 60]
for t_pc in [0, 29, 30, 59, 60, 90]:
    k_pc = sum(d_pc <= t_pc for d_pc in drops_pc)
    print(t_pc, round(s0_pc * decay_pc ** k_pc, 6));
```

:::

The step length stays fixed between drops <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
and falls by the factor $\decay$ exactly at $t = 30$ and $t = 60$.

<!-- no-figure: the example tabulates six step lengths -->

:::
